title: A note on beginnings and ends
text:
A note on beginnings and ends
• A sequence of words by itself does not indicate if it is a 
complete sentence or not
… four score and eight …
– Unclear if this is the start of a sentence, the end of a 
sentence, or both (i.e. a complete sentence)
• To make it explicit, we will add two additional symbols 
(in addition to the words) to the base vocabulary
– <sos>  :  Indicates start of a sentence
– <eos> : Indicates end of a sentence
38

title: A note on beginnings and ends
text:
A note on beginnings and ends
•
Some examples:
four score and eight
–
This is clearly the middle of sentence
<sos> four score and eight
–
This is a fragment from the start of a sentence
four score and eight <eos>
–
This is the end of a sentence
<sos> four score and eight <eos>
–
This is a full sentence
•
In situations where the start of sequence is obvious, the <sos> may not be needed, 
but <eos> is required to terminate sequences
•
Sometimes we will use a single symbol to represent both start and end of 
sentence, e.g just <eos> , or even a separate symbol, e.g. <s>

title: Story so far
text:
Story so far
• Language models model the probability of word (or symbol 
sequences) in the language
• This is typically performed in the form of next-symbol 
prediction
– Given the symbol sequence w0, w1, …, wk, it computes the 
probability distribution of the next symbol P(wk+1 | w0, w1, … , wk)
– This can be computed using a recurrent neural net
• They can be used both to compute the probability of a 
symbol sequence, or to conditionally generate/extend 
symbol sequences given an initial prompt

title: Pseudocode: Prune
text:
Pseudocode: Prune
# Note, there are smarter ways to implement this
function prune (state, score, beam, beamwidth)
sortedscore = sort(score)
threshold = sortedscore[beamwidth]
prunedstate = {}
prunedscore = []
prunedbeam = {}
bestscore = -inf
bestpath = none
for path in beam:
if score[path] > threshold:
prunedbeam += path # set addition
prunedstate[path] = state[path]
prunedscore[path] = score[path]
if score[path] > bestscore
bestscore = score[path]
bestpath = path
end
end
end
return prunedbeam, prunedscore, prunedstate, bestpath

title: Story so far
text:
Story so far
•
Language models model the probability of word (or symbol 
sequences) in the language, typically through next-symbol prediction
•
The “simple” sequence-to-sequence model for tasks such as machine 
translation are performed using an encoder-decoder model
– The encoder extracts a feature-representations for the input symbol 
sequence
– The decoder is a conditional language model that uses this 
representation to conditionally generate the output symbol sequence
– Inference is performed to find the most probable output sequence given 
the input sequence
•
The same mechanism can be used for other conditional generation 
tasks, such as image captioning, video captioning, etc.
